## Context

- Browsers benefit from explicit **security headers**: `Strict-Transport-Security`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options` / `frame-ancestors`, optional `Content-Security-Policy`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`.
- Today users set headers manually on `Response`; a **preset** reduces misconfiguration.
- See [Feature gaps](https://github.com/QueryaHub/OxyRoute/blob/main/docs/feature.md#4-безопасность-кроме-jwt).

## Direction

- Python helper: e.g. `SecurityHeadersConfig` → `dict[str, str]` merged into responses, or middleware that adds headers to all responses (careful with caching / CORS interaction).
- Document HSTS only over HTTPS and staging pitfalls.

## Acceptance criteria

- Pytest: response includes expected headers when helper is applied.
- Short `docs/security-headers.md` or section in `handlers.md`.

## Research

- MDN / OWASP secure headers; duplicate vs override policy with user `Response` headers.
